attributes.action: Allow bin helmets as a valid form of parliamentary attire.
attributes.additional_details: The House of Commons dress code forces elected MPs to conform to uniform business attire, erasing the unique identity voters endorsed. Whether Andy Burnham’s trademark black t-shirt or Count Binface’s bin helmet, removing these items disenfranchises voters who chose that specific persona. We demand the Speaker recognise campaign attire as valid parliamentary dress. Archaic rules should not override the democratic will to be represented authentically
attributes.background: Amend House of Commons dress code to explicitly permit bin helmets as valid attire for elected members. This ensures candidates elected on specific manifestos can represent their voters in the form in which they campaigned, upholding the democratic mandate over archaic sartorial traditions.

rejection.details: You may wish to sign this petition, which calls for similar action: "Review conventions relating to MPs’ dress in the Commons Chamber" https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/776476
